BEGINNING OF CONVERSATION: USER: I work in a restaurant and we have a rule about food that drops on the floor. If it hits the floor we throw it away. A lot of us think this is a stupid wasteful rule and use the food anyway as long as we think this is clean. Our manager fired a cook the other day for putting a steak on the grill after he dropped it on the floor/ how can we convince the manager that he made the wrong decision? ASSISTANT:

The restaurant should follow proper food safety protocols to minimize the risk of foodborne illness. Even if the food appears to be uncontaminated, it should still be discarded to avoid any potential health risks. Additionally, it is important to set a standard of respect for food and the environment. If the cook was disciplined for dropping food on the floor, then it is important for the manager to enforce the policy consistently to create a positive work environment.
